entries.note: Prepare candidate workspace/tool code and a probed immutable native executable before requesting the old view’s normal persistence/drain/exit-75 path. Preserve the previous workspace and binary until the replacement registers with a new view stamp. Failures enter recovering and become failed only after rollback completes; failed recovery is explicit. Keep old streams/HTTP mutations on their existing worker until drained. Serialize explicit updates, permit one automatic workspace crash recovery per explicit generation, and keep host-backed state/update control available if worker recovery fails. Never terminate/relaunch the original PTY host.

Opening an integration window requires a running agent from the originating root and an explicit absolute target directory. A durable window record is the only cross-root initial-agent exception. Repeat opens reuse that identity, closed views reopen their own layout, and graceful close never force-kills a session. The stable supervisor remains the sole writer for layouts/reports while workspace/tool workers can be replaced.

anchor.snippet: const notifyRetired = worker => { if (worker.child.connected) worker.child.send({ type: 'retired' }); };

entries.note: The supervisor's whole part in spec 095's Retirement: tell a replaced worker it was replaced, so it hands the token ledger and the feed to the worker that replaced it while its streams keep draining under spec 065. Sent where a retirement is committed - the finally that releases a replaced worker from `preserved`, and the rollback that retires a rejected candidate - and never at the swap, because a failed update restores the previous worker as the current one and a worker already told it was retired would then forward requests to itself. An older supervisor sends nothing and the worker behaves as it did before.
